displayPattern: 7-segment display on a *R9S96, *D9S96 or *R9S92 single-stage furnace in IOG-2037B (Goodman GR9S96, GD9S96 and GR9S92, and the Amana models in that same guide): EAF
meaning: Lost communication with the R-32 sensor: heating stops and only the fan runs because the furnace is in mitigation mode.
causes: Furnace not paired with an R-32 cooling unit
Loose or damaged R-32 sensor wire
R-32 sensor that the chart says to replace
diySteps: If the fan is running and the burners are not, write down EAF before you shut the furnace off
Technician: the chart says the furnace may not be paired with an R-32 cooling unit, and points to the R-32 information section of IOG-2037B
Technician: check that the R-32 sensor wire is connected and not damaged, and replace the R-32 sensor if that is what the chart calls for
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician. EAF is a sensor-communication fault in mitigation mode, not a thermostat fan setting.
